item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Russian strikes killed seven civilians in Ukraine and drones hit Moscow-area airports and a semiconductor plant in Oryol, while a daytime attack on Chernihiv civilian businesses killed one person and injured at least 25. Melania Trump brokered a local ceasefire in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, reducing fighting there, and a separate ceasefire was agreed for the same town. Ukraine reported that Starlink speed curbs persist despite promises to restore service. The conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

An Israeli airstrike hit a building in Nuseirat, Gaza, captured on video, while Israeli attacks on West Bank olive farmers have killed several farmers. Prime Minister Netanyahu has announced an extensive military operation and closure of the West Bank in response to the Hebron attack. The conflict produced 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

Saudi Arabia’s King Fahd airport was hit by missiles, killing one person and wounding eight, prompting the United States to order its personnel to leave Saudi Arabia and advise diplomats to depart. Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov visited Tehran and publicly backed Iran, hinting at possible Russian involvement as the United States and Israel draft plans for renewed strikes after the US midterm elections. Saudi Arabia is expanding a missile plant that may produce more powerful missiles. 123 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

Saudi-led coalition defenses continue to intercept missiles over Saudi territory and repel overnight attack waves. Yemeni forces reported more than a thousand strikes on Houthi positions in a single day, indicating intensified counter-offensive activity. NDTV notes the Houthis are employing a new weapon that is not a drone or missile. The conflict caused 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

Two Syrian security officers were killed in a raid on an ISIL cell near Damascus. Hundreds of Syrians protested repeated Israeli incursions while Syrian Christians faced heightened risk of killing or abduction. Jordanian and Syrian foreign ministers held expanded talks in Aqaba after attacks on churches in Jordan, and a US envoy noted that Syria's interim leader seeks Israel normalization. item.description:

item.title: Nigeria: the situation
item.description:
Gunmen killed an NSCDC officer and abducted a businessman in Plateau despite a curfew, and attacked an Ebonyi assembly candidate convoy, killing one and injuring three. In Benue, suspected herders killed three civilians and Senate leaders are demanding a security overhaul and troop deployment after 113 people were killed, while electricity workers withdrew services in Makurdi following an alleged attack. Bandits killed a NDC supporter in Enugu and continue to hold a widow, her son and a newborn captive three weeks after a kidnapping in Kaduna. Floods killed 245 people and displaced over 200,000, according to NEMA. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

The Kuki-Zo Women’s forum called for President’s Rule in Manipur, describing the crisis as political rather than security related. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: The Philippines: the situation
item.description:

The Philippines rescued four people on Hagonoy Island and its coast guard opened an upgraded station on Pag-asa Island, but coast guard personnel were killed and another wounded in a shooting in Cotabato City. Taiwan has expressed openness to cooperate with the Philippines on undersea cable protection and the Philippines is exploring deeper cooperation with Taiwan on this issue. An ex-NSA urged activation of the Philippines-China coast guard agreement. 176 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Ethiopia: the situation
item.description:
